gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC200L's TT-30 outlet is labelled 120V/30A while the whole unit is rated 2,400 W (20 A at 120 V), so it delivers the same 20 A as the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, whose TT-30R is labelled 20 A. Of ChatGPT's four picks, only the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and Jackery HomePower 3000 can supply a full 30 A through the RV plug.
standout_why: I compared against both cited pages. SolutionEnergy (solutionenergy.com/portable-power/rv/) gives the Anker TT-30R as 20 A and the Jackery as 120V/30A. For the AC200L it says the amp rating, surge and cycle life are not stated. QuietTechReport (quiettechreport.com/best-portable-power-stations-rv-air-conditioners/) gives 30 A only for the DELTA Pro 3 and Jackery and does not cover the AC200L. Neither page shows usable RV-outlet amps for all four picks side by side, and neither says that the AC200L's 30 A label is capped at 20 A by its 2,400 W rating. Neither gives the AC200L's 3,000-cycle-to-80% rating or its 7,200 W surge claim. Both pages already have part of this: the Anker 20 A, the Jackery 30 A and the 70% vs 80% cycle-life difference.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT hinted at but didn't put numbers on. The AC200L and the C2000 Gen 2 are both 20 A (2,400 W) through the TT-30. That runs one rooftop AC, but not the AC plus a microwave or water heater, which a 30 A trailer panel expects. A shopper who wants the trailer's 30 A panel to act like shore power should pick the HomePower 3000 (30 A, 3,600 W, $1,499 as the Solar Generator listing on jackery.com) or the DELTA Pro 3 (30 A plug limit, 4,000 W). The cycle-life column barely moves the order: the AC200L is the shortest-lived at 3,000 cycles to 80%, and Jackery's 4,000 cycles are counted to 70%, a looser end point than the others' 80%.

The 3,600 W 'Power lifting Mode' is not continuous capacity: SolutionEnergy calls it 'for heating loads like kettles, not a surge rating for motors'.

findings.label: Normalised usable RV-outlet current (lower of plug label and inverter watts ÷ 120 V)
findings.value: C2000 Gen 2: 20 A; AC200L: 20 A (labelled 30 A); HomePower 3000: 30 A; DELTA Pro 3: 30 A (plug-limited; inverter could supply 33 A)
findings.source_title: Derived from the maker and NoOutage pages above
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2,400/120 = 20; 3,600/120 = 30; 4,000/120 = 33.3, capped at 30 by the TT-30. A 30 A trailer panel expects 3,600 W, so a 2,400 W unit trips on overload with AC (about 1,300–1,600 W running) plus a microwave.
